intent: Bring reverse_survivors/src/core/types.ts (295 lines) under the repo-wide 250-line cap with no change to any stat value or type shape, completing reverse_survivors' move under the cap.
scope: reverse_survivors/src/core/types.ts — reduced to arena constants, difficulty tiers, director powers, edges, upgrades and the game-state shapes
reverse_survivors/src/core/enemies.ts — new: UnitKind, BossKind, EnemyKind, MoveMode, EnemySpec, ENEMY_SPECS, UNIT_ORDER, BOSS_ORDER, BOSS_UNLOCK_AT, BOSS_COOLDOWN
reverse_survivors/src/core/statusKinds.ts — new leaf: StatusKind, STATUS_ORDER, STATUS_POWER, STATUS_LABELS
14 import sites repointed across core, render and the test files
Non-goal: any stat value change, any symbol rename, any reordering of ENEMY_SPECS or the ORDER arrays
changes: Extracted the enemy roster — the kind unions, the EnemySpec shape, the 82-line ENEMY_SPECS stat table and the unit/boss orders, unlocks and cooldowns — into enemies.ts, which is the file to edit when balancing.

Extracted the status vocabulary into statusKinds.ts. This module is required rather than cosmetic: enemy specs name the status they inflict, and the survivor's state carries seconds-remaining per status, so leaving StatusKind in types.ts would have made types.ts and enemies.ts mutually dependent. statusKinds.ts imports nothing at all, so it is a true leaf.

Repointed 14 files with a scripted rewrite that splits each `from './types'` import across the three owning modules by symbol, rather than hand-editing 36 import sites. Six are test files; every edit is import-path-only, with no assertion or expected value changed.
Carried the ENEMY_SPECS and DIFFICULTIES blocks across verbatim, including the comments explaining why spawnKind is always a kind and why `normal` is the identity tier.

verification.command: npm run check (typecheck && eslint . --max-warnings 0 && vitest run --coverage)
verification.evidence: Test Files 13 passed (13); Tests 160 passed (160); Statements 100% (531/531), Branches 100% (159/159), Functions 100% (101/101), Lines 100% (514/514) — byte-identical totals to the baseline. This is the exact command reverse-survivors CI runs.
Built in 101ms, bundle 210.11 kB — exactly the pre-split baseline size. This is the second CI step and the gate that would expose an import cycle as a TDZ error.

verification.command: python3 comparison of every `name: number` pair across the old types.ts and the three new files, as sorted multisets
verification.evidence: 191 numeric pairs at baseline, 191 after, compared IDENTICAL. This is the check the test suite cannot make: a mistyped enemy hp or difficulty multiplier would still pass 160 tests and a 100% coverage gate, since the tests assert behaviour rather than pinning the balance table.

verification.command: grep of statusKinds.ts and enemies.ts import lines
verification.evidence: statusKinds.ts imports nothing; enemies.ts imports only `type { StatusKind } from './statusKinds'`; neither imports types.ts. The graph is acyclic.
types.ts 157, enemies.ts 143, statusKinds.ts 25 — all three under the 250-line cap, down from a single 295-line file.
No reverse_survivors file appears in the over-cap listing at all; this and the sim.ts split together clear the whole project.
All configured hooks pass on the touched files.

risks: types.ts remains the widest-imported module in the repo, and the split means some consumers now import from two or three modules where they previously imported from one. That is the cost of not leaving a re-export barrel, which the user explicitly asked for in this series.

The scripted rewrite classified symbols by name against two fixed sets. A symbol added to types.ts later would default to staying in types.ts, which is the safe direction, but the script is a one-off and is not committed.
statusKinds.ts is a very small module (25 lines). It exists to break a real cycle rather than for size, so it should not be folded back into types.ts even though it looks mergeable.
rollback: git revert the commit — 14 edited files, two added files, and no data, config or schema migration.
After rollback, re-run npm run check and npm run build; expect 160 tests passing at 100% coverage (531/159/101/514) and a successful build.
